questions.q: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{y}$, given that $y=3$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $y\,dy=x\,dx$. Integrate: $\dfrac{y^2}{2}=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$. Using $y=3,x=0$: $\dfrac{9}{2}=C$. So $y^2=x^2+9$, giving $y=\sqrt{x^2+9}$ (taking the positive root since $y=3>0$).
Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y}=2x\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=x^2+C$. So $y=Ae^{x^2}$ for some constant $A$. Using $y=5,x=0$: $A=5$. Solution: $y=5e^{x^2}$.

questions.q: A population $P$ grows at a rate proportional to its current size, modeled by $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP$. If the population doubles every 5 years, find $k$, to three decimal places.
questions.answer: Solving the DE: $P(t)=P_0e^{kt}$. Doubling: $2P_0=P_0e^{5k}$, so $e^{5k}=2$, giving $5k=\ln2$, $k=\dfrac{\ln2}{5}\approx0.139$.

questions.q: Newton's law of cooling states $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_a)$, where $T_a$ is ambient temperature. Solve this differential equation for $T(t)$ in terms of the initial temperature $T_0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dT}{T-T_a}=-k\,dt$. Integrate: $\ln|T-T_a|=-kt+C$. So $T-T_a=Ae^{-kt}$. At $t=0$, $T=T_0$, so $A=T_0-T_a$. Solution: $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=6$ using an integrating factor, given $y=1$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{\int2\,dx}=e^{2x}$. Multiply through: $e^{2x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2e^{2x}y=6e^{2x}$, i.e. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ye^{2x})=6e^{2x}$. Integrate: $ye^{2x}=3e^{2x}+C$, so $y=3+Ce^{-2x}$. Using $y=1,x=0$: $1=3+C$, so $C=-2$. Solution: $y=3-2e^{-2x}$.

questions.q: Use Euler's method with step size $h=0.5$ to estimate $y(1)$ for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x+y$, given $y(0)=1$, showing each step.
The differential equation $\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}=-\omega^2x$ describes simple harmonic motion. Verify that $x(t)=A\cos(\omega t)$ is a solution.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-A\omega\sin(\omega t)$. $\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}=-A\omega^2\cos(\omega t)=-\omega^2\left(A\cos(\omega t)\right)=-\omega^2x$, confirming $x(t)=A\cos(\omega t)$ satisfies the differential equation.

sections.heading: Family of solution curves and particular solutions

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2$, and explain what the arbitrary constant represents geometrically.
questions.answer: Integrating directly: $y=x^3+C$. The constant $C$ represents a vertical shift — the general solution is a whole family of curves, all with the same shape (since they share the same derivative $3x^2$ at every $x$), just shifted up or down by different amounts.

questions.q: A tank drains such that $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-k\sqrt{V}$ for some constant $k>0$, where $V$ is the volume of water. Solve this differential equation for $V(t)$, given $V(0)=V_0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dV}{\sqrt{V}}=-k\,dt$, i.e. $V^{-1/2}\,dV=-k\,dt$. Integrate: $2\sqrt{V}=-kt+C$. Using $V(0)=V_0$: $2\sqrt{V_0}=C$. So $2\sqrt{V}=-kt+2\sqrt{V_0}$, giving $\sqrt{V}=\sqrt{V_0}-\dfrac{kt}{2}$, so $V(t)=\left(\sqrt{V_0}-\dfrac{kt}{2}\right)^2$.

sections.heading: Verifying a solution to a second-order differential equation

questions.q: Verify that $y=e^{2x}$ is a solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}-5\dfrac{dy}{dx}+6y=0$.
A differential equation is given by $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x-y$. Find the gradient of the solution curve at the points $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, and $(1,1)$, and explain what a slope field represents.
questions.answer: At $(0,0)$: gradient $=0-0=0$. At $(1,0)$: gradient $=1-0=1$. At $(1,1)$: gradient $=1-1=0$. A slope field is a diagram that plots a short line segment of the correct gradient at many points in the plane, without solving the equation explicitly — sketching a solution curve then amounts to drawing a curve that follows the direction of the segments at every point it passes through.

sections.heading: Solving a linear differential equation with an initial condition

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{y}{x}=x$ for $x>0$ using an integrating factor, given $y=2$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Rewrite in standard form: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{1}{x}y=x$. Integrating factor: $e^{\int-\frac{1}{x}dx}=e^{-\ln x}=\dfrac{1}{x}$. Multiply through: $\dfrac{1}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{1}{x^2}y=1$, i.e. $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=1$. Integrate: $\dfrac{y}{x}=x+C$, so $y=x^2+Cx$. Using $y=2,x=1$: $2=1+C$, so $C=1$. Solution: $y=x^2+x$.

questions.q: A population $P$ grows according to the logistic differential equation $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP(10-P)$. Using the partial fraction decomposition $\dfrac{1}{P(10-P)}=\dfrac{1}{10P}+\dfrac{1}{10(10-P)}$, solve for $P$ in terms of $t$, given $P(0)=1$ and leaving $k$ as an unknown constant.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dP}{P(10-P)}=k\,dt$. Integrate the left side using the given decomposition: $\dfrac{1}{10}\ln|P|-\dfrac{1}{10}\ln|10-P|=kt+C$, i.e. $\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\left|\dfrac{P}{10-P}\right|=kt+C$. Using $P(0)=1$: $\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)=C$. So $\ln\left|\dfrac{P}{10-P}\right|=10kt+\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)$, giving $\dfrac{P}{10-P}=\dfrac{1}{9}e^{10kt}$. Solving for $P$: $9P=(10-P)e^{10kt}$, so $P(9+e^{10kt})=10e^{10kt}$, giving $P=\dfrac{10e^{10kt}}{9+e^{10kt}}$.

sections.heading: Checking the order and degree of a differential equation

questions.q: State the order of each of the following differential equations: (a) $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-2y$, (b) $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+4\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=0$, (c) $\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3}=\sin x$.
questions.answer: The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest derivative present. (a) Only a first derivative appears, so this is a first-order differential equation. (b) The highest derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, so this is second-order. (c) The highest derivative is $\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3}$, so this is third-order.

sections.heading: Using Euler's method with a smaller step size

questions.q: Use Euler's method with step size $h=0.25$ to estimate $y(0.5)$ for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x$, given $y(0)=1$, showing each step, and compare with the exact solution $y=x^2+1$.
questions.answer: Euler's method: $y_{n+1}=y_n+h\cdot f(x_n,y_n)$. Step 1 ($x_0=0,y_0=1$): $y_1=1+0.25(2\cdot0)=1+0=1$. Step 2 ($x_1=0.25,y_1=1$): $y_2=1+0.25(2\cdot0.25)=1+0.125=1.125$. Estimate: $y(0.5)\approx1.125$. Exact solution: $y(0.5)=(0.5)^2+1=1.25$. The Euler estimate underestimates the true value, since the method uses the derivative only at the start of each interval rather than accounting for how the derivative changes within it.

questions.q: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$ for $x>0$, given $y=6$ when $x=2$, and describe the family of curves this represents.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y}=\dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=\ln|x|+C$, so $y=Ax$ for some constant $A$. Using $y=6,x=2$: $6=2A$, so $A=3$. Solution: $y=3x$. This represents the family of straight lines through the origin; the particular solution satisfying the initial condition is the specific line with slope $3$.

questions.q: A cup of coffee at $90^\circ$C is placed in a room at ambient temperature $20^\circ$C. Using Newton's law of cooling, $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$, and given that after $10$ minutes the coffee has cooled to $60^\circ$C, find the value of $k$ to three decimal places.
questions.answer: Using $T_a=20$, $T_0=90$, and $T(10)=60$: $60=20+(90-20)e^{-10k}$, so $40=70e^{-10k}$, giving $e^{-10k}=\dfrac{4}{7}$. Taking natural logs: $-10k=\ln\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)\approx-0.5596$, so $k\approx0.056$.

questions.q: This question has three parts. A tank initially contains $200$ litres of pure water. Salt water containing $3$ grams of salt per litre flows in at a rate of $2$ litres per minute, and the well-mixed solution flows out at the same rate, so the volume stays constant at $200$ litres. Let $S(t)$ be the amount of salt (in grams) in the tank at time $t$ minutes. (a) Explain why $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=6-\dfrac{S}{100}$. (b) Solve this differential equation for $S(t)$, given $S(0)=0$. (c) Find the amount of salt in the tank after $50$ minutes, to the nearest gram.
questions.answer: (a) Salt flows in at a rate of $3$ grams/litre $\times2$ litres/minute $=6$ grams/minute. Salt flows out at a rate proportional to the current concentration $\dfrac{S}{200}$ grams/litre, times the outflow rate of $2$ litres/minute, giving $\dfrac{2S}{200}=\dfrac{S}{100}$ grams/minute out. Net rate: $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=6-\dfrac{S}{100}$. (b) This is a linear first-order DE. Integrating factor: $e^{\int\frac{1}{100}dt}=e^{t/100}$. $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(Se^{t/100}\right)=6e^{t/100}$. Integrating: $Se^{t/100}=600e^{t/100}+C$, so $S=600+Ce^{-t/100}$. Using $S(0)=0$: $0=600+C$, so $C=-600$. Solution: $S(t)=600\left(1-e^{-t/100}\right)$. (c) At $t=50$: $S(50)=600\left(1-e^{-0.5}\right)=600(1-0.6065)=600(0.3935)\approx236$ grams.
